the eight projected ring radii, normalized to the innermost and compared as SQUARED ratios so no square root of the closed form is ever taken

Legs.Subject: SymmetryWord.Apply(node) for twelve words of every length one through eight

Legs.Shared: SymmetryLattice.Reflect, the identical member - Create composes it once per node at bake time, the test composes it again per node; this catches a baked table wired to the wrong node, letter order or orbit slot, never a wrong reflection

Legs.Subject: for every one of the twelve words Apply is a permutation of all 240 nodes (no two nodes share an image); OrbitLength(node) is the count iteration measures until the node recurs; the counted Apply(node, steps) equals that iteration at every step from 0 to twice the orbit length and at the same steps offset by minus three orbit lengths; Apply(node, Order) and Apply(node, -7 * Order) are the node; Order is the least common multiple of the measured orbit lengths; IsIdentity holds exactly at Order one; [3,3] is the identity
the Order of every one of the twelve words

Legs.Subject: SymmetryLattice.InnerProduct at every node: the count of other nodes pairing to -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2

Legs.Subject: every argument outside the documented domain is REFUSED rather than aliased onto one inside it: an order below one or past thirty-one, a coordinate at or past 2^order, a distance at or past 4^order. Nine cases, each of which previously returned a value: C# masks a shift count, so an order of 32 became a shift of zero and collapsed the grid to a single cell -- Decode(32, 12345), Decode(1, 4) and Decode(1, 0) all returned (0, 0), and Encode(1, 2, 0) matched Encode(1, 0, 0). A bijective spatial key that maps distinct inputs together absorbs the caller's corruption instead of surfacing it

the domain is REACHABLE at both edges -- order one at its far corner and far distance, and order thirty-one at coordinate 2^31 - 1 and distance 2^62 - 1 -- so the refusals above bound the domain rather than shrink it

no public member of SymmetryLattice returns a collection a published marshal can unwrap into the process-wide backing array; a consumer's write to the value it IS handed does not survive to the next read; and the index bound refuses at both ends while staying reachable at the last position. Made by ATTEMPTING the escape rather than by reading a declared type, which is the error that let the first repair look complete: read-only is not ownership and neither is immutable. A ReadOnlyMemory yields its backing array to MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray and an ImmutableArray yields the same array to ImmutableCollectionsMarshal.AsArray -- both public, neither needing reflection or unsafe code, and either one let a consumer zero verified lattice metadata for every later consumer in the process. Count-and-index returning a value type by copy is the only shape with no route back
